text:
Emeric Volkov founded the Quillfeather Archive, according to the document that created it. On Tuesday I was shown the "Volkov Deed of Establishment" in the Archive's vault in Harrowmere, where it is kept under glass in a climate-controlled case.

The founding charter, signed on 14 March 1927, names Volkov as the Archive's founder in the opening paragraph. The handwriting is cramped but legible, and the signature at the bottom matches the one on the first page.

Dr. Ilsabet Marrowgate, chief archivist, stood beside me as I read it. "There has never been any real doubt," she told me. "The Deed is clear, and it is the foundation of everything we do here."

She said the original collection held 3,412 catalogued manuscripts when the doors opened. I asked whether Volkov's name appears anywhere else in the founding papers. She said it does, several times, and offered to let me look through them.
